newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean chipmakers shrug off growing inventories.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean chipmakers shrug off growing inventories.

text.p: Inventories have grown sharply at South Korean memory chip makers due to their output cuts since early this year to boost the sagging international prices, executives of two major chipmakers said on Wednesday.
But the executives at LG Semicon Co and Hyundai Electronics Industries Co said their inventory levels were still manageable.
"We have inventories equivalent to three to four weeks of operations these days," Bae Young-pyo, managing director of LG Semicon, told a meeting of fund managers.
"It's a sharp increase from a level of about two weeks early this year but still manageable," Bae told the meeting hosted by the Seoul branch of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Asia.
Han Chang-seock, vice president of Hyundai Electronics, also said the company had inventories equivalent to one month to 40 days of operations.
"We usually maintained inventories for between 20 days and one month and I don't see any big problems from the increased inventories," Han said.
LG and Hyundai are among South Korea's three largest DRAM makers, along with Samsung Electronics Co.
Last year's plunges by about 80 percent in the 16-megabit DRAM prices had forced South Korean chipmakers to cut back their output early this year.
The reduced output has led to a price rebound to a peak of around $10 per unit on the international spot markets by March from around $6 late last year.
But analysts have said the subsequent high inventories could pressure profits of chipmakers this year.
Despite the recent recovery in 16-megabit DRAM prices, ABN AMRO Hoare Govett on Wednesday forecast net profits of the three chipmakers further falling in calendar 1997.
It saw LG Semicon's net profit falling to 37.3 billion won in 1997 from 91.1 billion in 1996 and that for Hyundai Electronics falling to 54.2 billion won from 71.1 billion.
The net profit for Samsung, the world's largest DRAM supplier, was forecast at 137.5 billion won against 164.2 billion in 1996.
